claims.head: Tilted ice, toward the Canucks’ net
claims.body: The Golden Knights have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Canucks the worst. Expect the Golden Knights to spend more of the night in the Canucks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

VAN.head: The Canucks have their work cut out
VAN.body: Even though Vegas will be without Hanifin, the Golden Knights have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Canucks’ best hope is keeping shots to a minimum, plus a big night from Leevi Meriläinen.

story.head: The Canucks are desperate for a win
paras: The Canucks are on a seven-game losing streak, and the Golden Knights (13-5-3) lost 3-2 in a shootout to Nashville on Friday. The Knights won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in Vancouver on Oct 4. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Golden Knights second in the Pacific (fourth in the NHL).

The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.167) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .335, and their goaltending has held them back. The Golden Knights’ record (.690) is about what their chances are worth.
In their seven-game skid, the Canucks have been outscored 30-14, including 18-9 at 5-on-5.

The Canucks have had shaky goaltending (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). They also have a leaky penalty kill (32nd), so the Golden Knights’ power play (4th) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded. Vancouver has allowed 4.52 goals a game, the most in the league. On the other side, the Golden Knights have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and create chances on the penalty kill (2nd). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Elias Pettersson (#40) (5 G / 16 A / 21 P in 21 GP) leads the Canucks in scoring, and Brock Boeser (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 21 GP) has a team-high seven goals. For the Golden Knights, Jack Eichel (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Mark Stone (10 G / 10 A / 20 P in 21 GP) has a team-high ten goals.

Leevi Meriläinen (2-9-1 / .885 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Vancouver. Vegas has two options in net: Adin Hill (7-2-1 / .907 SV% in 10 GS) and Carter Hart (6-3-2 / .896 SV% in 11 GS). Hill has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
